hint.label: Salamander’s Life Cycle

atoms.b: A salamander’s life cycle begins with laying eggs.
In the next stage, salamanders are called larvae. In this stage, the salamander larva lives in water and doesn’t have limbs yet.
In this stage, the larva starts to develop limbs and lungs. This transformation is important for its future on land.
In the final stage of its life cycle, the salamander climbs out of the water and lives the rest of its life on land.

atoms.a: The word amphibian can be translated as “double life”. This word is very fitting because amphibians spend the first part of their lives in water and the second part on land.
The life cycle of amphibians is similar to mammals because they always look exactly the same while growing into adulthood.
Amphibians experience metamorphosis while growing up.
Amphibians’ bodies go through drastic changes in their life cycles.
